$comment: The workload profiles the load harness runs (SEE-99, docs/development/load.md).
They are data rather than code so that the numbers behind docs/testing/see-99.md can be
read without reading Go, and so that asking 'what happens at four times the payload' is an
edit rather than a rebuild. Every field is documented in docs/development/load.md, every
field a profile leaves out has a default in tools/loadtest/internal/drive/profile.go, and a
misspelled one is refused rather than silently defaulted.
The counts here are what a laptop can hold while still measuring something: the ramp is the
profile that climbs, and it is the one that answers 'how far does this machine go'.

profiles.name: hot
profiles.note: one shared channel, every listener on it — the fan-out case a popular feed is

profiles.name: spread
profiles.note: eight publishers with a channel each, and listeners holding two feeds apiece

profiles.name: mixed
profiles.note: everything at once: revisions, withdrawals, manifest changes, snapshot walks and hints

profiles.name: slow
profiles.note: a fast, fat feed, so a listener that stops reading has something to fall behind on

profiles.name: ramp
profiles.note: the hot channel, climbing toward ten thousand listeners until a stage cannot hold

profiles.name: shared-address
profiles.note: four hundred listeners behind one address, as a building full of phones would be
